vendor_company: Oracle Corporation (NetSuite was acquired by Oracle in November 2016 for ~$9.3B)
target_segment: Mid-market to enterprise (typical minimum ~10 users; common deployment in companies $5M-$1B+ revenue)
target_vertical: Horizontal cloud ERP — manufacturing, wholesale distribution, multi-channel retail/DTC brands, software/services, professional services, nonprofits; very strong in product-centric enterprises (NetSuite is a Leader in 2025 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Cloud ERP for both Service-Centric and Product-Centric Enterprises)
pricing_model: Annual subscription = base license + per-user fees + optional module fees + (optionally) revenue-based or transaction-based tiers; quote-only via NetSuite sales or partners
starting_price_usd: Approx $999/month base license + ~$99-$149/user/month; reported all-in entry ~$1,500-$2,500/month for 10 users; total cost varies widely with modules
free_trial_or_freemium: No public free trial or freemium tier; product tours and guided demos only (free trial not offered for the core ERP)
shopify_supported: Native (official Oracle/NetSuite Connector, formerly FarApp, acquired by Oracle April 2021); also widely supported by third-party SuiteApps (Celigo, Folio3, NetScore, Pipe17, APPSeCONNECT, Webbee)
shopify_app_rating: 4.2 / 5 (Shopify App Store, 'NetSuite ERP Connector' by Oracle)
shopify_install_count: ~7 reviews on Shopify App Store (very low — most NetSuite-Shopify deployments are configured inside NetSuite via the SuiteApp, not installed from the Shopify App Store, so review count under-represents real install base)
shopify_built_for_shopify_badge: No (NetSuite ERP Connector by Oracle does not hold the Built for Shopify certification) [uncertain]
shopify_plus_partner_status: [uncertain] — NetSuite Connector supports Shopify Plus stores, but I could not confirm a Shopify Plus Certified App Partner directory listing for Oracle's official connector
shopify_sync_direction: Bi-directional: products/pricing/inventory NetSuite -> Shopify; orders/customers/fulfillment updates Shopify -> NetSuite; tracking/fulfillment NetSuite -> Shopify
shopify_synced_entities: Products, variants/options, pricing, inventory, sales orders, customers, fulfillments (tracking numbers, carriers, shipping methods), refunds; B2B catalogs/companies (via Shopify Plus B2B); POS orders including BOPIS and ship-from-store
shopify_service_item_support: [uncertain] — NetSuite supports non-inventory and service items natively, but explicit documentation that the NetSuite Connector syncs Shopify service/non-physical items as service items in NetSuite was not confirmed in this research
shopify_multi_store_support: Yes — multiple Shopify stores per NetSuite tenant supported (documented as 'Multi-Store Support' in NetSuite Connector)
shopify_pos_support: Yes — Shopify POS orders import to NetSuite; supports POS Pro features 'Buy online, pick up in-store' (BOPIS) and 'Buy in-store, ship to customer'; multi-location inventory propagates to Shopify POS
shopify_b2b_catalog_support: Yes — NetSuite Connector supports Shopify B2B (Shopify Plus) storefronts including B2B pricing; company hierarchies and custom pricing catalogs syncable (some scenarios use partner connectors like Pipe17 for richer B2B mapping)
shopify_markets_support: [uncertain] — Shopify Markets-specific pricing/duties/landed-cost handling in the official NetSuite Connector is not clearly documented in public sources
shopify_metafield_to_erp_field_mapping: [uncertain] — NetSuite Connector supports custom field mapping (NetSuite Saved Search Export and custom field configuration), but no first-class out-of-box metafield mapping UI like Brightpearl's is documented
shopify_variant_option_mapping: Variants map to NetSuite matrix items / item options; SKU is the primary key; variant-level inventory and pricing are supported
shopify_real_time_or_batch: Hybrid — real-time order sync via Shopify webhooks (documented: 'Setting Up Real-Time Order Sync for Shopify in NetSuite Connector'); inventory and other entities can run real-time or at configurable batch intervals (commonly every 5-15 min)
shopify_known_limitations: Complex initial setup and configuration; users describe the connector as 'difficult to manage' on Shopify App Store; low public review count; many advanced flows require add-on charges (e.g., FBA inbound); customizations beyond standard flows typically require partner/SuiteScript work; legacy connector occasionally lags behind newest Shopify B2B/Markets features so customers fall back on Celigo or partner SuiteApps; only 7 public Shopify App Store reviews
etsy_supported: Third-party (no Oracle-native Etsy connector in the same form as Amazon/Shopify); supported via SuiteApps/iPaaS partners including Celigo, Yuju Marketplace, Codisto-style multichannel apps, and SPS Commerce
etsy_native_or_third_party: Third-party — NetSuite Connector (FarApp) does not list Etsy as a first-class storefront; Etsy is reached via partner SuiteApps or iPaaS connectors (e.g., Celigo, Yuju, multichannel marketplaces)
etsy_listing_creation_vs_sync_only: Depends on third-party connector — most partner connectors support both create and sync of Etsy listings; this is not built into the native Oracle NetSuite Connector [uncertain]
etsy_inventory_sync: Via partner SuiteApp (Celigo / Yuju etc.) — inventory levels sync from NetSuite outward to Etsy on configurable schedules; details depend on which partner connector is licensed [uncertain]
etsy_order_import: Via partner SuiteApp — orders import to NetSuite as sales orders or cash sales on schedule (typically 5-60 min polling) or via partner webhooks [uncertain]
etsy_synced_entities: Through partner SuiteApps: listings, variations/inventory, orders, fulfillments/tracking, refunds/cancellations [uncertain — exact set depends on chosen partner connector]
etsy_known_limitations: No native Oracle SuiteApp for Etsy; customers must select and pay for a third-party SuiteApp; Etsy-specific handling for personalization, made-to-order lead times, and digital products varies by partner; not the typical NetSuite use case (Etsy sellers are usually too small for NetSuite)
amazon_supported: Native (official NetSuite Connector for Amazon Seller Central and Amazon Vendor Central; SuiteApp bundle 169116). Also extensively supported by third-party SuiteApps (Celigo Amazon-NetSuite, Folio3, NetScore, SuperSync/Netgain, APPSeCONNECT, InfiPlex)
amazon_marketplaces: All major Amazon marketplaces: US, CA, MX, BR, UK, FR, IT, ES, DE, NL, SE, PL, TR, AE, IN, JP, AU, SG, CN (NetSuite Connector documents US, CA, UK, FR, IT, ES, DE, JP, CN as supported; partner SuiteApps cover the full SP-API marketplace list)
amazon_seller_types: FBA (AFN), FBM (MFN), and dual-listing of the same SKU on both; Vendor Central also supported by NetSuite Connector (separate connector module); Seller Fulfilled Prime automation supported
amazon_synced_entities: Listings (item details), pricing, inventory, sales orders, fulfillments (carrier/tracking), settlement reports (fees, payouts, refunds), MCF (Multi-Channel Fulfillment) inventory adjustments, FBA inbound shipments, returns
amazon_listing_creation: Yes — NetSuite Connector can create and update Amazon listings (item details, pricing, quantity) from NetSuite item records; advanced listing creation/optimization typically uses partner SuiteApps like NetScore or Folio3
amazon_repricing_support: Not included in core NetSuite Connector — handled via third-party repricers (e.g., RepricerExpress, BQool, Aura) integrated separately [uncertain]
amazon_buy_shipping: [uncertain] — NetSuite Connector does not document an in-app Amazon Buy Shipping label purchase flow comparable to Veeqo's; Amazon Buy Shipping integration is typically left to FBM-via-Amazon labels or third-party shipping connectors
amazon_fba_inbound_workflow: Supported as an add-on feature (additional fees apply): inbound shipments imported into NetSuite as transfer orders; the FBA shipment plan ID is placed on a designated field; item fulfillment and item receipt are created automatically based on Amazon's inbound shipment status
amazon_sp_api_inbound_v2024_03_20: [uncertain] — NetSuite Connector has migrated from legacy MWS to SP-API as Amazon mandated through 2024, but I could not confirm whether the FBA inbound flow specifically uses the new Fulfillment Inbound v2024-03-20 API; partner connectors like InfiPlex advertise SP-API inbound support
amazon_settlement_report_handling: NetSuite Connector imports Amazon Settlement Reports and maps each fee or transaction line (sales, FBA fees, referral fees, refunds, ad spend, reserves) to NetSuite accounts or items; settlement reconciliation posts to the general ledger as journal entries or itemized cash sales/refunds
amazon_marketplace_facilitator_tax_handl: Marketplace-facilitator collected tax is captured from settlement reports and journaled separately so it is not recognized as the seller's tax liability; exact mapping is configurable per marketplace [uncertain in detail]
amazon_multi_account_support: Yes — multiple Amazon seller accounts and multiple marketplaces can be connected into a single NetSuite tenant for unified global e-commerce reporting
amazon_known_limitations: FBA inbound and some advanced features are paid add-ons; setup complexity is high (token-based auth, SuiteCloud features, SP-API credentials); rate limits on SP-API can throttle high-volume sellers; community frequently switches to Celigo or partner SuiteApps for more flexibility; settlement reconciliation can require custom GL mapping work
xero_supported: Third-party / partner-built — Xero is NOT a typical ongoing accounting integration for NetSuite (NetSuite IS the ledger). Xero connections to NetSuite are almost always one-time data-migration projects from Xero -> NetSuite, performed via iPaaS (Celigo, Skyvia, Stitch, Boomi) or partner migration services (Zone & Co, ScaleNorth, SuiteMigration, Anchor Group)
xero_app_store_certified: No — there is no official NetSuite SuiteApp on the Xero App Store, nor a Xero-certified NetSuite app from Oracle; Xero-listed connectors target migration tooling rather than ongoing sync
xero_app_awards_recognition: No — not applicable (Oracle/NetSuite does not pursue Xero Global App Awards)
xero_synced_entities: In migration scenarios only: chart of accounts, customers, vendors/suppliers, items, historical invoices, bills, payments, journal entries, opening balances; no ongoing transactional sync is the standard pattern
xero_accounting_sync_mode: Not applicable — NetSuite is the GL of record. Where hybrid/parallel runs exist during transition, integration is typically summary-journal or invoice-per-order via iPaaS (Celigo/Skyvia/Boomi)
xero_cogs_journal_method: Not applicable — NetSuite computes COGS internally (perpetual moving-average / standard / LIFO/FIFO depending on item costing method); Xero is not in the loop post-cutover
xero_multi_currency: Not applicable (no ongoing Xero posting); NetSuite itself is multi-currency
xero_tracking_category_mapping: Not applicable as an ongoing sync; during one-time migration, Xero tracking categories typically map to NetSuite Classes, Departments, or Locations
xero_tax_handling: Not applicable as ongoing sync; migration maps Xero tax rates to equivalent NetSuite tax codes / nexus configurations
xero_known_limitations: There is no official Oracle-built Xero connector. Customers migrating from Xero typically use partner data-migration services (typical 1-2 weeks for simple data, 6-8 weeks for multi-entity, $25K-$150K+ implementations). Ongoing bi-directional sync is rare and only seen in transition periods or unusual hybrid architectures
qb_online_supported: Third-party — same pattern as Xero. QuickBooks Online -> NetSuite is overwhelmingly a one-time migration (Celigo offers a free QBO->NetSuite migration template; SuiteMigration, ScaleNorth, Paystand, Anchor Group, Seibert Consulting all provide QB->NetSuite migration services). Ongoing QBO sync is uncommon and configured via iPaaS (Celigo, Boomi)
qb_desktop_supported: Third-party / migration-only — QuickBooks Desktop -> NetSuite migrations are common; ongoing sync uses iPaaS (Celigo, Boomi, eOne SmartConnect) when needed
qb_app_certified: No official Oracle SuiteApp listed on the Intuit App Store (QuickBooks App Store); Intuit App Store does carry third-party migration tools
qb_synced_entities: In migration: chart of accounts, customers, vendors, items, historical invoices, bills, payments, journal entries, opening balances; in rare ongoing sync scenarios (Celigo): items, vendors, customers, sales receipts, invoices
qb_accounting_sync_mode: Not applicable as ongoing sync (NetSuite IS the GL). When hybrid parallel runs exist, Celigo's QB-NetSuite template offers 12 pre-built flows that operate as transactional sync (invoice-per-order style)
qb_cogs_journal_method: Not applicable — NetSuite computes COGS natively; QB is not in the loop post-cutover
qb_multi_currency: Not applicable for ongoing sync; NetSuite OneWorld supports multi-currency natively
qb_class_location_mapping: Not applicable for ongoing sync; in migration, QBO Class and Location dimensions map to NetSuite Class, Department, Location, or Subsidiary fields
qb_known_limitations: No first-party Oracle connector. Migrations cost $25K-$150K and take 1-6 months. Most customers run QuickBooks for 1-6 months in parallel via Celigo before full cutover, then retire QuickBooks. Bi-directional ongoing sync is rare; most customers go full NetSuite once migrated
other_ecom_channels: NetSuite Connector (FarApp) natively supports: Shopify / Shopify Plus, Amazon Seller Central, Amazon Vendor Central, eBay, Walmart, BigCommerce, Adobe Commerce (Magento), WooCommerce. Other channels (TikTok Shop, Wix, Squarespace, Faire, Square, custom storefronts) are reached via SuiteApp partners (Celigo, Yuju, Pipe17, NetScore, Folio3) or NetSuite's own SuiteCommerce platform
bundle_kit_component_decomposition: Yes — NetSuite supports Kit/Package items and Assembly items; when a Kit sells, components decrement automatically; Assembly items decrement components on Build / Work Order completion. Multi-level BOMs cascade decrements through subassemblies
other_accounting_integrations: NetSuite IS the ledger — it does NOT typically integrate with other accounting systems as an ongoing sync. Sage 50, Sage Intacct, Zoho Books, MYOB, FreshBooks, Wave are all replaced by NetSuite in the typical implementation. Migration tooling and consulting partners exist for each (Celigo, Boomi, eOne, Skyvia, partner migration services). NetSuite OneWorld is the multi-entity / multi-currency / multi-subsidiary version used by enterprises with global operations
bom_support: Yes — full bill of materials module with BOM creation, revisions/versions, where-used, cost roll-ups, and item-level BOM linking
multi_level_bom: Yes — multi-level / nested BOMs with bottom-up build (subassemblies built before parent assemblies); MRP cascades net requirements down through all BOM levels
production_orders: Yes — Work Orders / Assembly Builds; with WIP & Routings: work centers, routings, operation tasks, labor costing, infinite-capacity scheduling, and Gantt-chart drag-and-drop. SuiteApps for Advanced Manufacturing extend with shop-floor control
batch_lot_tracking: Yes — lot/batch numbers tracked from raw material receipt through production to finished goods shipment, with expiry, FEFO picking, and traceability reporting (when WMS or Lot tracking module is enabled)
serial_tracking: Yes — full serial number tracking; barcode-scan capture on receiving, picking, fulfillment, and returns (with WMS or Advanced Inventory)
bin_location_support: Yes — bin-level inventory tracking within warehouses via NetSuite WMS; supports directed putaway, directed picking, bin replenishment, and locations-without-bins for smaller warehouses/retail
multi_warehouse: Yes — unlimited multiple physical locations / warehouses / subsidiaries; OneWorld extends to multi-subsidiary and multi-country
barcoding: Yes — supports GS1-128 (1D) and GS1 DataMatrix (2D) including GTIN-14 and HIBC formats; mobile label printing of item, GTIN, quantity, UoM, lot, expiry, and serial number via NetSuite WMS
purchase_orders: Yes — full PO module with partial receipts, multi-currency, supplier price lists, drop-ship, special order, blanket POs, approval workflows
supplier_management: Yes — vendor records with lead times, supplier-SKU mapping, multiple vendor-item relationships, supplier price lists, MOQs, item preferred vendor, vendor performance reporting
landed_cost_support: Yes — landed cost on item receipts: freight, duty, insurance, brokerage, handling allocated to inventory cost using weight, value, quantity, or manual basis; allocated landed cost flows into per-unit cost and COGS
multi_currency_inventory_valuation: Inventory is valued in the subsidiary's base currency; purchasing can be transacted in foreign currency with FX gain/loss handled at receipt and bill; NetSuite OneWorld supports per-subsidiary base currencies. True per-currency inventory valuation is not standard
ai_demand_forecasting: Yes — NetSuite Demand Planning forecasts inventory needs from historical demand, seasonality, open opportunities, and sales forecasts. Intelligent Performance Management (IPM) in NetSuite Planning & Budgeting layers ML on top for continuous monitoring. NetSuite 2025.2 added Contextual Insights AI to NetSuite Analytics Warehouse
ai_purchase_order_suggestions: Yes — NetSuite Demand Planning generates reorder/replenishment recommendations that can be turned into POs or transfer orders; AI-assisted PO suggestions extend this further in newer releases [uncertain on exact 2025.2 PO drafting features]
ai_natural_language_query: Yes — SuiteAnalytics Assistant is NetSuite's AI-driven natural-language query tool (in active rollout 2025) — users generate reports and dashboards using plain-English prompts instead of saved searches or SuiteQL
public_api: Yes — SuiteTalk REST (modern JSON, OAuth 2.0 + Token-Based Auth, default for new integrations as of 2025; expanding coverage release by release), SuiteTalk SOAP (legacy; 2025.2 is the last regularly scheduled SOAP release), SuiteQL (SQL-like query API), and RESTlets (custom SuiteScript-built REST endpoints)
webhook_event_coverage: No native outbound webhooks — webhooks are implemented via SuiteScript User Event Scripts / RESTlets that POST to external endpoints on record create/update/delete. Common pattern is to use middleware/iPaaS to decouple. New TBA-based integrations cannot be created from 2027.1 — OAuth 2.0 mandatory
integration_architecture: Native SuiteApps (FarApp/NetSuite Connector and partners) + heavy iPaaS ecosystem (Celigo is the de facto standard, alongside Boomi, MuleSoft, Workato, Jitterbit); SuiteCloud Development Framework (SDF) for custom SuiteApps; SuiteScript for in-tenant logic; SuiteFlow for low-code workflows
zapier_make_support: Yes — Zapier has a NetSuite integration (limited triggers/actions vs SuiteTalk REST); Make.com (Integromat) also offers NetSuite modules. Most production integrations skip Zapier/Make in favor of Celigo or SuiteScript [uncertain on n8n]
mobile_app: Yes — NetSuite mobile app (iOS and Android) for approvals, expense capture, time entry, dashboards, CRM record access, and basic transactional views
mobile_barcode_scanning_app: Yes — NetSuite WMS mobile app (and SuiteApps like RF-SMART, NetScore WMS Mobile) provide native handheld barcode scanning for receiving, putaway, picking, packing, fulfillment, cycle count, and shipping
rate_limit_handling_documented: Partially — NetSuite documents its own concurrency governance (SuiteCloud Plus, concurrency limits); rate-limit handling for Shopify / Amazon SP-API / Xero / QBO is handled inside the FarApp/NetSuite Connector and partner connectors and is documented in SuiteApp-specific docs rather than centrally [uncertain on completeness]
sync_frequency: Shopify: real-time webhooks for orders + 5-15 min polled inventory; Amazon: hourly order polling typical + near-real-time for some events; Xero/QBO: migration only (one-time or scheduled batches via iPaaS); other channels: configurable per SuiteApp (5 min - hourly common)
shipping_carrier_integrations: Native built-in: FedEx, UPS, USPS/Endicia (real-time rates + label printing); via SuiteApps and partners: DHL, Royal Mail, Australia Post, Canada Post, LTL carriers, and many regional carriers (RF-SMART Shipping, Descartes ShipRush, Shiptheory, ShipStation, Shippo)
shipping_label_buying: Yes — native in-NetSuite shipping label generation for FedEx/UPS/USPS using registered carrier accounts; tracking numbers saved to item fulfillment. Third-party SuiteApps extend to more carriers and rate-shopping
three_pl_integrations: Yes — via SuiteApp partners and iPaaS: ShipBob, ShipHero, Extensiv (3PL Central), Logiwa, Deliverr, FBA-as-3PL (MCF), Flexport, ShipMonk, Whiplash; NetSuite is one of the most-integrated ERPs in the 3PL ecosystem
edi_support: Yes — SPS Commerce, TrueCommerce, B2BGateway, Crossfire, Data Masons, OmniLogic, Cleo all offer SuiteApps for EDI (X12, EDIFACT) supporting retail compliance with Walmart, Target, Amazon Vendor, etc.
g2_rating: 4.1 / 5 on G2 (Oracle NetSuite ERP); thousands of reviews [uncertain on exact current review volume]
g2_grid_quadrant: Leader — also recognized as a Leader in 2025 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Cloud ERP for Service-Centric Enterprises and Cloud ERP for Product-Centric Enterprises
capterra_rating: 4.2 / 5 on Capterra based on 1,761 reviews (1,473 positive, 192 neutral, 96 negative); Ease of Use 3.9, Customer Service 3.8, Value-for-Money 3.8, Functionality 4.2
notable_customers: Used by tens of thousands of companies globally including Shaw Industries, Cameron's Coffee, Sezzle, GoPro (historically), Land O'Lakes (selected modules), Williams-Sonoma (selected), Roku, Lovesac, Vivint, Allbirds (historically), Lucid Motors, and many more — NetSuite reports 41,000+ customers across 217 countries [uncertain on most recent customer count]
last_major_release: NetSuite 2025.2 (Fall 2025) — introduced Contextual Insights (AI analytics in NetSuite Analytics Warehouse), SuiteAnalytics Assistant rollout, IPM enhancements, and was the last regularly scheduled SOAP web services endpoint release. NetSuite 2026.1 in active rollout as of May 2026 [uncertain on exact 2026.1 GA date]
owner_parent_company: Oracle Corporation (acquired NetSuite for ~$9.3 billion USD in November 2016; NetSuite operates as Oracle's Global Business Unit headquartered in Austin, TX)
last_funding_event: Acquired by Oracle, November 2016, ~$9.3 billion USD; no subsequent funding events (now an Oracle business unit)
public_status_page_uptime: https://status.netsuite.com/ — public status dashboard; historical uptime not aggregated as a single SLA percentage on the public page, but NetSuite contracts include 99.5%+ uptime commitments [uncertain on current rolling uptime]
